faq.q: Can French Bulldogs fly on planes?
faq.a: Some can fly in the cabin if they meet the airline's rules and fit comfortably in an approved under-seat carrier. Cabin and cargo acceptance varies by route, aircraft, carrier and dog.

faq.q: Can French Bulldogs fly as checked pets or cargo?
faq.a: Many airlines restrict brachycephalic dogs in checked baggage or cargo because of breathing and heat risks. Ask your airline for its current policy before you book; do not assume another carrier has identical rules.

faq.q: Will a French Bulldog fit under an airplane seat?
faq.a: A small dog may fit, but it must have adequate space in an airline-approved carrier that fits the aircraft's under-seat dimensions. Check the exact aircraft and cabin policy; a weight limit alone is not enough.

faq.q: Should I sedate my French Bulldog before a flight?
faq.a: Do not use sedatives or tranquilizers on your own. Discuss fitness to fly, medications, heat risk and airway symptoms with your veterinarian well ahead of travel.

faq.q: What documents does a dog need to enter the United States?
faq.a: Under current CDC rules, a dog entering or returning to the U.S. generally needs to appear healthy, be at least six months old, have a readable microchip and a CDC Dog Import Form receipt. More documents are required after travel to certain high-risk rabies countries; check the CDC Dog Importation Navigator.
